text:
maria: FYI I pulled perf dashboards after the kernel-priority change and we're seeing a sustained ~9% throughput drop on H100 p99 and ~6% on A100 for long-context Llama-variant requests. noticed it around 13:42 UTC when the rollout hit canary.

kai: ugh. do we have a profiler trace? what changed in kernel-priority exactly?

maria: kernel-selector now prefers fused-attn-v2 for sequences > 1024; fallback weights changed. commit: 8f2c9b2. here's a quick sampled profiling summary:
```
model: llama-13b
device: H100
before: 15477 tokens/s (p50 2.6ms, p99 18ms)
after: 14097 tokens/s (p50 2.7ms, p99 20.5ms)
kv-frag-rate: before 0.8% -> after 4.6%
batch-formation avg tokens: before 3.2k -> after 2.1k
```

tom: kv fragmentation jump looks suspicious — fused kernel seems to reduce effective packing? could be mismatch in kv cache stride meta used by the kernel swap.

vlad: also queueing: the continuous-batcher windowing is using the same soft token cap per-gpu. If effective token-per-batch falls, the scheduler opens more slices -> more small batches -> worse kernel throughput.

maria: proposed quick triage options:
- revert kernel-priority on canary
- bump per-gpu soft token cap for H100/A100 by +40% (temporary)
- add a kernel-fit filter to avoid switching to fused-attn-v2 when kv-frag > 2%

kai: +1 to the kernel-fit filter. Can we detect frag cheaply in the admission path? we already emit kv-frag telemetry per request.

tom: we can compute a running frag ratio in the batcher; cheap add. patch idea:
```
if device in [H100, A100] and kv_frag_ratio > 0.02:
    prefer kernel_family = 'legacy-attn'
else:
    keep existing selector
```

maria: also saw a perf-regression trace where per-device batch token target dropped from 3200 -> 2100 for H100 due to new token-budget smoothing. might be overaggressive smoothing params.

vlad: so likely two interacting factors: kernel selection causing packing inefficiency + smoothing lowering token budgets -> smaller batches. both multiply.

kai: quick experiment plan:
1) flip kernel-fit guard in canary
2) bump H100/A100 soft token cap to 4k for 1h
3) run profiler 5-min traces and compare p99/p50 + kv-frag

maria: deploying plan 1 now to canary. i'll post logs. infra-bot: deploy canary kernel-priority-guard -> success @ 13:56 UTC :rocket:

infra-bot: canary deploy finished for kernel-priority-guard (job id: job-7729). monitoring watch started.

maria: initial canary numbers look promising — H100 tokens/s up ~7% vs 'after' baseline and kv-frag dropped to 1.3%.

tom: good sign. tl;dr: avoid blind kernel preference shifts without validating packing/kv-frag and batcher smoothing coupling. need a presubmit perf regression test that simulates high-kv-frag patterns.

vlad: agreed. i'll open a follow-up to add a regression check and a perf-playbook note for kernel swaps + batcher params.

kai: please add a short rollback runbook in the PR: exact flags to revert and telemetry keys to watch (kv_frag_ratio, batch_tokens_avg, p99_latency).

maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
